contributions.statement: When evaluating agents or harness changes on tasks mined from your own repo history, rebuild each task repo as a single commit (no future git objects), delete hidden tests from the workspace and block code-host egress while allowing package registries; without this, one model's score was inflated by 21 points through answer leakage.
contributions.evidence: Table 3: GLM-5.2 78.80 -> 57.32 under anti-hacking controls, DeepSeek-V4-Pro 49.98 -> 49.11; Table 4: 186 PASS->FAIL vs 15 FAIL->PASS (McNemar p<0.001); Table 5: local answer-file access 103 -> 0, network 49 -> 0. Single run per condition; blocklist gaps admitted.

contributions.statement: Under-specified constants, defaults, ordering and signatures in task statements cause false agent failures, so acceptance criteria should pin them explicitly.
contributions.evidence: Table 10: 21 FAIL->PASS vs 2 PASS->FAIL on 102 refined instances, but 32/35 churn on 629 unrefined instances shows ~10% single-run noise, and refinements often reveal test-expected constants.

reason: Adds a measured magnitude and model-dependence to the known git-history/egress leakage problem, directly applicable to any in-house agent eval mined from the team's repos.
